The National Pension Commission (PenCom) has disclosed that the pension industry has committed N241 billion to an infrastructure development fund aimed at channelling long-term pension capital into Nigeria’s infrastructure sector.

The commitment, made through the Pension Industry Infrastructure Consortium established by the Pension Industry Leadership Council, PILC, in collaboration with FSD Africa, is expected to rise to over N300 billion as additional pledges come in.

Speaking at a press briefing in Lagos, the director-general of PenCom, Omolola Oloworaran, said the initiative represents the industry’s first major step to mobilise pension funds for infrastructure, offering long-term, inflation-protected assets that match retirement savings.

She clarified that the N241 billion is a commitment and not yet invested, with framework development, agreement with FSD Africa and appointment of a fund manager expected to be concluded before deployment by Q2 2027.

Oloworaran added that the industry is engaging development partners who could match the committed capital, potentially growing the fund beyond its current target.

She said the Consortium was established in conjunction with FSD Africa earlier in the year and represents the first step in a deliberate effort by the industry to play in the infrastructure space.

“As of today, pension funds have committed a total of N241 billion, and we expect that to touch almost N300 billion very soon as we get all the commitments in,” the DG said.

According to her, the industry is working with a clear timetable, with the signing of an MOU with FSD Africa and appointment of a fund manager expected between now and Q1, 2027 while the first tranche of investments should be deployed by Q2 2027.

The PenCom DG noted that developmental partners are also expected to match what the industry has put forward, which could significantly increase the pool available for infrastructure.

She stressed that the decision to invest in infrastructure was not by compulsion, but a voluntary decision by all Pension Fund Administrators (PFAs) in the best interest of contributors.

The PFAs, she said, reviewed the opportunity and realized infrastructure offers higher returns and a potential hedge against inflation, which is why every single PFA in the industry has contributed to the fund.

She described the infrastructure gap in Nigeria, saying that the pension industry hopes to continue to contribute meaningfully, generate employment and improve livelihoods.
